heroHeadline: Bamako Siege Day 40: Africa Corps Deploys Lancet Drones; Mali Announces $3.5M Bounty on JNIM Leader Iyad Ag Ghali
heroSubtitle: Day 40 of JNIM's declared 'total siege' of Bamako (announced April 28, 2026). Africa Corps released video of the first confirmed Lancet loitering munition strike in Mali on June 2 — targeting a pickup truck in Nazarak, Tombouctou Region — and has also deployed FPV kamikaze drones; but Military Africa (June 2026) reports that JNIM and IS-Sahel insurgents are simultaneously conducting their own drone strikes on Africa Corps/FAMa positions in the Gao-Ménaka-Ansongo corridor, making northern Mali's airspace contested on both sides. The Mali junta announced a 2 billion CFA ($3.5M USD) bounty on JNIM emir Iyad Ag Ghali and 1.5 billion CFA ($2.5M) on Katiba Macina commander Amadou Koufa around June 5 — the first formal leadership bounty program in the 14-year conflict, with additional rewards for FLA commander Alghabass Ag Intalla. Burkina Faso's 23rd Rapid Reaction Squad eliminated 10 militants in Bangassugu (June 5-6), seizing 9 motorcycles and 10 machine guns. ACTIVE FRONTS (June 7): (1) BAMAKO BLOCKADE (Day 40): 3 of 6 supply roads cut; motorcycle ban (Decree 2026-0312) in force since June 3; Africa Corps BMP-3 road-clearance operations; food prices +43–65% above pre-siege baselines; WFP suspended ($620M gap); IRC: 5.1M Malians need aid; FAO projects 52.8M at IPC Phase 3+ in June–August lean season; no renewed JNIM escalation in post-Eid window but structural blockade unchanged. (2) KIDAL FRONT (Day 42): FLA retains Kidal; aerial interdiction campaign ongoing with Lancet and FPV drones; FLA chief: 'Kidal is only the beginning.' (3) BURKINA FASO: Imam Mohamed Kindo remains detained without charges since May 26; Grand Mosque still closed; no new major JNIM atrocity confirmed in June 5–7 window following record May 2026 campaign (~300+ killed). (4) HUMANITARIAN EMERGENCY: 15.4M face IPC Phase 3+ food crisis June–August (OCHA June 3) — only 19% of $3.7B required funding received.
